steps.note: the triangle landed and the Pen is STILL the tool in hand, with the new path picked so it can be repainted without putting the Pen down
the first anchor of the next shape lets the last one go: drawing is not editing, and a shape still picked is a shape a stray Backspace can take off the canvas behind the line you are drawing
Backspace mid-path takes back ONE anchor, the same step Command Z takes, and the finished triangle is untouched: still two layers
two shapes for one press of P: the second triangle was drawn without picking the Pen up again, which is what an icon of five shapes needs
one press of Escape with nothing being drawn puts the Pen down and hands back to Select with the last shape still picked: the way out that is not the tool bar

one Undo takes back the whole second shape, however many anchors went into it. It is the action step rather than Command Z because a walk's window is never active, so the chord never reaches the Edit menu (undo-shortcut-walk is the walk about that)
V still puts the Pen down mid-path, exactly as it always did, and the two anchors that were on screen were never in the document, so nothing was added and there is nothing to undo

the second anchor of a short edge arrives as a DOUBLE click, because it is a click close to the last one in space and time. It has to land as an anchor: the window used to take it and zoom itself instead, so the shape came out with one corner missing. Three anchors here is the proof it landed
